claim: SARS-CoV-2 has among the largest genomes of any RNA virus, encoding for 29 proteins.
source: The β-coronavirus, Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome CoronaVirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has among the largest genomes of any RNA virus (Bar-On et al., 2020; Hartenian et al., 2020), encoding for 29 proteins.
evidence: Supported by citations to Bar-On et al., 2020 and Hartenian et al., 2020

claim: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a was postulated to be a viroporin based on its membrane localization, oligomerization, and C-terminal sequence similarities to a calcium ATPase from Plasmodium falciparum and an outer-membrane porin from Shewanella oneidensis.
source: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a was postulated to be a viroporin based on its membrane localization, oligomerization, and C-terminal sequence similarities to a calcium ATPase from Plasmodium falciparum and an outer-membrane porin from Shewanella oneidensis (Lu et al., 2006; Yu et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lu et al., 2006 and Yu et al., 2004

claim: K+-selective currents were recorded from SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a-expressing Xenopus laevis oocytes.
source: Recording K+-selective currents from SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a-expressing Xenopus laevis oocytes were interpreted to mean that SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a was a viroporin (Lu et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lu et al., 2006

claim: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a current was inhibited by 5–50 µM emodin.
source: This current was inhibited by 5–50 µM emodin, a natural compound suggested as a potential SARS-CoV-1 antiviral (Lu et al., 2006; Schwarz et al., 2011), and by 10 mM BaCl2, a nonspecific K+ channel blocker.
evidence: Supported by citations to Lu et al., 2006 and Schwarz et al., 2011

claim: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a current was inhibited by 10 mM BaCl2, a nonspecific K+ channel blocker.
source: This current was inhibited by 5–50 µM emodin, a natural compound suggested as a potential SARS-CoV-1 antiviral (Lu et al., 2006; Schwarz et al., 2011), and by 10 mM BaCl2, a nonspecific K+ channel blocker.
evidence: Supported by citations to Lu et al., 2006 and Schwarz et al., 2011, and established knowledge about BaCl2

claim: Whole-cell patch-clamp of SARS-CoV-1 expressing HEK293 cells exhibited non-selective ion currents blocked by BaCl2 that were attributed to SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a.
source: Whole-cell patch-clamp of SARS-CoV-1 expressing HEK293 cells exhibited non-selective ion currents blocked by BaCl2 that were also attributed to SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a (Chan et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chan et al., 2009

claim: Orf3a promotes host cell death and causes intracellular vesicle formation and Golgi fragmentation during SARS-CoV-1 infection.
source: Comparison of viral infections between wild-type and Orf3a-deficient SARS-CoV-1 strains demonstrates that Orf3a promotes host cell death and causes intracellular vesicle formation and Golgi fragmentation (Freundt et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Freundt et al., 2010

claim: During SARS-CoV-1 infection, Orf3a stimulates the production of mature IL-1β, a marker of NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
source: In addition, during SARS-CoV-1 infection, Orf3a stimulates the production of mature IL-1β, a marker of NLRP3 inflammasome activation (Siu et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Siu et al., 2019

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aHALO colocalizes with the plasma membrane marker farnesylated-GFP.
source: After 24 h expression, SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aHALO colocalized with the PM marker, farnesylated-GFP, which was further supported by total internal reflection microscopy (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-C

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aHALO partially colocalizes with markers of the endocytic pathway, including early endosomes (EEA, Rab5), late endosomes (Rab7) and lysosomes (LAMP1).
source: We also observe partial colocalization of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aHALO with markers of the endocytic pathway, including EE (EEA, Rab5), LE (Rab7) and the Lyso (LAMP1) compartments (Figure 1D–F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, C-E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, C-E

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a shows minimal localization in the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, and peroxisomes.
source: Minimal SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is seen in all other subcellular compartments tested (Figure 1G–I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F) consistent with other reports (Ghosh et al., 2020; Gordon et al., 2020a; Zhang et al., 2020; Miao et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G-I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F, and citations to Ghosh et al., 2020; Gordon et al., 2020a; Zhang et al., 2020; Miao et al., 2021

claim: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3aHALO displays a similar subcellular distribution as SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a, colocalizing with markers of the endocytic pathway and at the plasma membrane.
source: For SARS-CoV-1 Orf3aHALO, we identify a similar trend of colocalization with markers of the endocytic pathway and at the plasma membrane (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: No ionic current densities distinct from control cells were observed in HEK293 cells expressing SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aSNAP in K+, Na+, Cs+, NMDG+, and Ca2+ external solutions.
source: In all external cationic bath solutions that we tested, including K+, Na+, Cs+, N-methyl-D-glucamine (NMDG+), and Ca2+, we were not able to observe ionic current densities distinct from those measured in control cells (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-C

claim: No distinct K+, Na+, Ca2+, or H+ currents were recorded from endolysosomal vesicles in HEK293 cells expressing SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aHALO compared to untransfected endolysosomal vesicles.
source: No distinct K+, Na+, Ca2+, or H+ currents were recorded as compared to those measured from untransfected endolysosomal vesicles (Figure 2D–I, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D-I and Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aGFP localizes to the plasma membrane of A549 cells.
source: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aGFP localizes to the plasma membrane of A549 cells, yet we were unable to measure ion currents (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2

claim: No ion currents were measured from A549 cells expressing SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aGFP.
source: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aGFP localizes to the plasma membrane of A549 cells, yet we were unable to measure ion currents (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP localizes to the plasma membrane of Xenopus oocytes.
source: We were not able to record SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP ionic currents above background (Figure 2J–L, Figure 2—figure supplement 3), despite confirmation of PM localization of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP in Xenopus oocytes by surface biotinylation (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A

claim: No SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP ionic currents above background were recorded from Xenopus oocytes in high potassium solution (96 mM KCl) or standard TEVC recording solutions (ND96, 96 mM NaCl).
source: We were not able to record SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP ionic currents above background (Figure 2J–L, Figure 2—figure supplement 3), despite confirmation of PM localization of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP in Xenopus oocytes by surface biotinylation (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J-L and Figure 2—figure supplement 3

claim: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a localizes to the plasma membrane in Xenopus oocytes and HEK293 cells.
source: Although we confirmed SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a PM localization in both expression systems, we recorded no currents attributable to the expressed protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 3; Lu et al., 2006; Chan et al., 2009; Schwarz et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 3

claim: No currents attributable to SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a were recorded from Xenopus oocytes and HEK293 cells.
source: Although we confirmed SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a PM localization in both expression systems, we recorded no currents attributable to the expressed protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 3; Lu et al., 2006; Chan et al., 2009; Schwarz et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 3

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a likely assembles as a 64 kDa dimer in cell membranes.
source: We first evaluated the oligomeric state of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP in cell membranes by chemical crosslinking and concluded that it likely assembles as a 64 kDa dimer (Figure 3—figure supplement 3I).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3I

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a in LE/Lyso environment was determined to 3.0 Å resolution.
source: Despite its challenging size for cryo-EM structural determination (<100 kDa), we were able to resolve a nearly identical conformation of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a in both nanodisc preparations, determined to 3.0 Å in the LE/Lyso environment or 3.4 Å in the PM environment (global RMSD 0.34 Å, Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplements 1–5, Supplementary file 1, Nygaard et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplements 1–5, and citation to Nygaard et al., 2020

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a in PM environment was determined to 3.4 Å resolution.
source: Despite its challenging size for cryo-EM structural determination (<100 kDa), we were able to resolve a nearly identical conformation of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a in both nanodisc preparations, determined to 3.0 Å in the LE/Lyso environment or 3.4 Å in the PM environment (global RMSD 0.34 Å, Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplements 1–5, Supplementary file 1, Nygaard et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplements 1–5, and citation to Nygaard et al., 2020

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a structures in LE/Lyso and PM environments have a global RMSD of 0.34 Å.
source: Despite its challenging size for cryo-EM structural determination (<100 kDa), we were able to resolve a nearly identical conformation of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a in both nanodisc preparations, determined to 3.0 Å in the LE/Lyso environment or 3.4 Å in the PM environment (global RMSD 0.34 Å, Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplements 1–5, Supplementary file 1, Nygaard et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by experimental data and citation to Nygaard et al., 2020

claim: Cryo-EM density for SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is well-resolved between serine 40 and valine 237.
source: Cryo-EM density for SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is well-resolved between serine 40 and valine 237, whereas the electron density for the distal N- and C-termini, and a loop within the C-terminus (residues 175–180), is poor or not present.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from cryo-EM analysis

claim: The electron density for the distal N- and C-termini, and a loop within the C-terminus (residues 175–180) of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a, is poor or not present.
source: Cryo-EM density for SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is well-resolved between serine 40 and valine 237, whereas the electron density for the distal N- and C-termini, and a loop within the C-terminus (residues 175–180), is poor or not present.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from cryo-EM analysis

claim: The overall architecture of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is a dimer comprised of six transmembrane helices, three provided by each subunit.
source: The overall architecture of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is a dimer and is comprised of six transmembrane (TM) helices, three provided by each subunit, with dimensions of 50 Å in diameter and 70 Å in height (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B

claim: SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a has dimensions of 50 Å in diameter and 70 Å in height.
source: The overall architecture of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is a dimer and is comprised of six transmembrane (TM) helices, three provided by each subunit, with dimensions of 50 Å in diameter and 70 Å in height (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B

claim: The SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a N-terminus is positioned towards the extracellular or luminal space and its C-terminus within the cytosol.
source: Due to the odd number of TM helices per subunit, the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a N-terminus is positioned towards the extracellular or luminal space and its C-terminus within the cytosol, as previously reported for SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a (Figure 3B–C; Lu et al., 2006; Tan et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-C and citations to Lu et al., 2006 and Tan et al., 2004

claim: TM2 and TM3 of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a have pronounced tilting of >30° from a line perpendicular to the membrane.
source: When viewed from the extracellular/luminal side, TM1–3 are arranged in clockwise manner with pronounced tilting of TM2 and 3 (>30°) from a line perpendicular to the membrane (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B

claim: TM2 and TM3 of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a are 45 Å in length and hydrophobic.
source: Helical tilting is likely required for TM2 and 3, which are 45 Å in length, hydrophobic, and would otherwise unfavorably protrude from the membrane.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from structural analysis

claim: TM1 of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is 30 Å in length.
source: TM1 is shorter by comparison (30 Å) and extends through the remainder of the lipid bilayer by a structured loop that connects with TM2.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from structural analysis

claim: TM2 and TM3 of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a are positioned at a 30° angle with respect to one another.
source: Although tilted at a similar angle in the membrane, TM2 and 3 are positioned at a 30° angle with respect to one another (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B

claim: The cytosolic domain of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is assembled from a cluster of eight β-sheets (β1–8) contributed by each subunit.
source: Extending from TM3 is a 104 amino acid structured cytosolic domain assembled from a cluster of eight β-sheets (β1–8) contributed by each SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a subunit, forming a compact and continuous molecular surface that protrudes 30 Å into the cytosol (Figure 3B–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-C

claim: The cytosolic domain of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a protrudes 30 Å into the cytosol.
source: Extending from TM3 is a 104 amino acid structured cytosolic domain assembled from a cluster of eight β-sheets (β1–8) contributed by each SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a subunit, forming a compact and continuous molecular surface that protrudes 30 Å into the cytosol (Figure 3B–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-C

claim: The dimer interface within the cytosolic domain of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a has a buried surface interface of 1010 Å2 per subunit.
source: These extensive interactions along the dimer interface within the cytosolic domain (buried surface interface of 1010 Å2 per subunit) appear integral to the integrity of the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a dimer (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C

claim: The narrowest point in the transmembrane region of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is ~0.8 Å radius, which is too narrow to accommodate a dehydrated cation.
source: Approximately two-thirds of the TM region is tightly packed in its current conformational state, with the narrowest point in this region (~0.8 Å radius) too narrow to accommodate a dehydrated cation (Figure 3D–E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D-E

claim: Two distinct clusters of polar residues are present in the transmembrane region of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a: T89, S92, H93, Y109, Y113 positioned towards the extracellular or luminal space, and Q57, N82, Q116, N119 situated within the center of the membrane.
source: Two distinct clusters of polar residues, the first positioned towards the extracellular or luminal space (T89, S92, H93, Y109, Y113) and the second situated within the center of the membrane (Q57, N82, Q116, N119) are regions that may accommodate hydrophilic ions or molecules (Figure 3F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F

claim: The transmembrane region of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a contains a ~12 Å diameter aqueous vestibule positioned above the cytosolic domain.
source: The final approximately one-third of the TM region positioned above the cytosolic domain contains a ~12 Å diameter aqueous vestibule which is accessible from the cytosol through two narrow portals.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from structural analysis

claim: The aqueous vestibule of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is accessible from the cytosol through two narrow portals with 1.5 Å radius.
source: The final approximately one-third of the TM region positioned above the cytosolic domain contains a ~12 Å diameter aqueous vestibule which is accessible from the cytosol through two narrow portals. Although the portal could permit the movement of partially hydrated cations (1.5 Å radius), the composition of residues lining the aqueous vestibule is highly basic (K61, K75, H78, R122, R126) creating a positively-charged region that would not be suitable for cations (Figure 3D–E and G–H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D-E and G-H

claim: The aqueous vestibule of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is lined by highly basic residues (K61, K75, H78, R122, R126) creating a positively-charged region that would not be suitable for cations.
source: Although the portal could permit the movement of partially hydrated cations (1.5 Å radius), the composition of residues lining the aqueous vestibule is highly basic (K61, K75, H78, R122, R126) creating a positively-charged region that would not be suitable for cations (Figure 3D–E and G–H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D-E and G-H

claim: Two distinct lateral fenestrations within the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a transmembrane region expose the aqueous vestibule to the lipid bilayer: one formed between the structured loop of TM1 and TM3 (Lipid Site 1) and one between TM2 and TM3 (Lipid Site 2).
source: Within the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a transmembrane region are two distinct lateral fenestrations that expose the aqueous vestibule to the lipid bilayer formed between the structured loop of TM1 and TM3 (Lipid Site 1) and between TM2 and TM3 (Lipid Site 2) (Figure 4A–C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: Each fenestration in SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a is filled with tubular density attributable to lipids.
source: Each fenestration is filled with tubular density attributable to lipids (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: DOPE was modeled into Lipid Site 1 of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a based on the size, shape, and presence of density in both PM and LE/Lyso lipid compositions.
source: We modeled a 1,2-Dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphatidylethanolamine (DOPE) molecule into Lipid Site 1 based on the size, shape, and presence of this density in both PM and LE/Lyso lipid compositions (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: R122 in SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a stabilizes the phospholipid phosphate group in Lipid Site 1.
source: A notable arginine residue (R122) located in TM3 neighbors both lipid sites and, in its current conformation, stabilizes the phospholipid phosphate group in Lipid Site 1 (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B

claim: Both fenestrations in SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a are unlikely to be occupied by DOPE simultaneously because their positively-charged headgroups are in proximity (~5 Å) to one another and R122 clashes with Lipid Site 2.
source: It is unlikely that both fenestrations would be occupied by DOPE at once since their positively-charged headgroups are in proximity (~5 Å) to one another and R122 clashes with Lipid Site 2 (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C

claim: The cryo-EM structure of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a in a LE/Lyso lipid Saposin A-containing nanodisc was determined to 2.8 Å resolution.
source: We determined the cryo-EM structure of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a in a LE/Lyso lipid Saposin A-containing nanodisc to 2.8 Å resolution (Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and Supplementary file 1

claim: The overall architecture and conformational state of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a in Saposin A-containing nanodiscs are nearly identical to the structures in MSP1D1-containing nanodiscs, with a global RMSD of 0.50 Å.
source: Its overall architecture and conformational state are nearly identical to the structures of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a in MSP1D1-containing nanodiscs, harboring a TM constriction and a basic aqueous vestibule (global RMSD 0.50 Å, Figure 4—figure supplement 3I).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3I

claim: Saposin A binds directly to SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a in a similar region to where MSP1D1 binds, but with a slightly different interface.
source: We observe a direct interaction of Saposin A with SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a, which occurs in a similar region to where MSP1D1 is binding, but with a slightly different interface of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: In the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a Saposin A nanodisc structure, Saposin A binding occludes Lipid Site 1 and electron density is absent from this site.
source: Comparison of the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a MSP1D1 and Saposin A nanodisc structures reveals several differences which can be attributed to scaffold protein binding. The binding of the Saposin A to SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a directly occludes Lipid Site 1 and consequently, electron density is absent from this site.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from structural comparison

claim: In the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a Saposin A nanodisc structure, R122 is rotated 135° from the MSP1D1 structure and occludes Lipid Site 1, creating space for a lipid to occupy Lipid Site 2.
source: Instead, we observe a 135° rotation of R122 into Lipid Site 1, where its side chain is directly interacting with Saposin A, creating space for a lipid to occupy Lipid Site 2 (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: The cryo-EM structure of SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a in a LE/Lyso-like membrane MSP1D1 nanodisc was determined to 3.1 Å resolution.
source: To further address the possibility of a functional and evolutionary distinction between SARS-CoV-2 and SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a, we determined the structure of SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a in a LE/Lyso-like membrane MSP1D1 nanodisc to 3.1 Å resolution and compared it to the SARS-CoV-2 homolog (Figure 4—figure supplements 3–5, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 3–5 and Supplementary file 1

claim: The overall architecture and conformational state of SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a are nearly identical to the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a cryo-EM structures, with a global RMSD of 0.47 Å.
source: Its overall architecture and conformational state are nearly identical to the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a cryo-EM structures (global RMSD 0.47 Å, Figure 4—figure supplement 3J).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3J

claim: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a does not have an obvious pore in its current conformational state.
source: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a does not have an obvious pore in its current conformational state, and its aqueous vestibule is also electrostatically positive (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5

claim: The aqueous vestibule of SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a is electrostatically positive.
source: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a does not have an obvious pore in its current conformational state, and its aqueous vestibule is also electrostatically positive (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5

claim: Neither SARS-CoV-1 nor SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a are viroporins.
source: In combination with our extensive efforts to identify and reproduce SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a currents in various expression systems without success, we conclude that both Orf3a homologs are not viroporins.
evidence: Supported by extensive electrophysiology data and structural analysis

claim: No K+ or Cl- transport was observed from SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP reconstituted at high (1:10, 1:25) or standard (1:100, wt:wt) protein to lipid ratios using an ACMA fluorescence-based flux assay.
source: We did not observe any K+ or Cl- transport using a 9-Amino-6-Chloro-2-Methoxyacridine (ACMA) fluorescence-based flux assay (Figure 5B–C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B-C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C

claim: No reduction in light scattering was observed with SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP-containing vesicles compared to vesicle control using a 90° light-scattering K+ flux assay.
source: Compared to the vesicle control, no reduction in light scattering is observed with SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP-containing vesicles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E-G

claim: Large single channel-like conductances were observed in symmetrical K+, Na+ and Ca2+ from SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP vesicles reconstituted at a high (1:10), but not standard (1:100), protein to lipid ratio.
source: Our attempts to record macroscopic currents were unsuccessful, yet we observed large single channel-like conductances in symmetrical K+, Na+ and Ca2+ from SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP vesicles reconstituted at a high, but not standard, protein to lipid ratio (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-C

claim: The large single channel conductances observed from vesicle-reconstituted SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a at high protein to lipid ratios likely result from transient membrane leakiness or ion channel protein contamination, not SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a activity.
source: Although these conductances are consistent to what has been recently published, we believe that these data likely result from transient membrane leakiness or ion channel protein contamination, and not due to SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a activity (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B–C; Kern et al., 2021; Accardi et al., 2004; Niu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B-C and citations to Kern et al., 2021; Accardi et al., 2004; Niu et al., 2021

claim: Voltage-dependent anion channels 1–2 (VDAC1–2) were identified by mass spectrometry in proteoliposome-reconstituted SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a samples.
source: We performed mass spectrometry using proteoliposome-reconstituted SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a. The only ion channel proteins that appeared on this list were the voltage-dependent anion channels 1–2 (VDAC1–2), outer membrane mitochondrial proteins that are large-conducting, non-selective channels which can be blocked by 4,4'-Diisothiocyano-2,2'-stilbenedisulfonic Acid (DIDS) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D–F; Thinnes et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2D-F and citation to Thinnes et al., 1994

claim: Some of the currents recorded from proteoliposome-reconstituted SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a were blocked by 100 μM DIDS, suggesting contribution by VDAC.
source: We asked if some of the currents that we record could be blocked by DIDS. After 1 min of application of the vehicle (DMSO), we observed channel block by 100 μM DIDS, which could be recovered by a washout of the inhibitor, suggesting that some of the current that we measure may be contributed by a VDAC (Figure 5—figure supplement 2E–F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2E-F

claim: An accumulation of Rab7 puncta is observed in HEK293 cells expressing SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aHALO, but not in uninduced control cells.
source: In doxycycline-treated HEK293 cells expressing SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aHALO, we observe an accumulation of Rab7 puncta, which is not observed in uninduced, control cells, suggesting a defect in HOPS complex-mediated vesicle fusion (Figure 6A and J; Miao et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2021; Qu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A and J, and citations to Miao et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2021; Qu et al., 2021

claim: Rab7 puncta are not observed after doxycycline-induced expression of SARS-CoV-1 Orf3aHALO.
source: In contrast, we do not observe the Rab7 puncta after doxycycline-induced expression of SARS-CoV-1 Orf3aHALO, suggesting an evolutionary distinction between these two homologs (Figure 6B and K; Miao et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2021; Qu et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and K, and citations to Miao et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2021; Qu et al., 2021

claim: VPS39GFP elutes with SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP in a concentration-dependent manner in co-immunoprecipitation experiments.
source: We observed an enrichment of VPS39GFP that was SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP concentration dependent (0.5–50 μg protein; Figure 6C), but very little to no binding was observed when performing the co-IP with all concentrations of SARS-CoV-12x-STREP Orf3a (50 μg shown; Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C

claim: Very little to no binding of VPS39GFP was observed with SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a2x-STREP in co-immunoprecipitation experiments.
source: We observed an enrichment of VPS39GFP that was SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP concentration dependent (0.5–50 μg protein; Figure 6C), but very little to no binding was observed when performing the co-IP with all concentrations of SARS-CoV-12x-STREP Orf3a (50 μg shown; Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C

claim: An unstructured loop between β3–4 of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a could be facilitating the VPS39 interaction.
source: By inspecting the cytosolic domain of both Orf3a cryo-EM structures and by pinpointing the divergent regions of amino acid sequence conservation, we identified an unstructured loop between β3–4 that could be facilitating the VPS39 interaction (Figure 6D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D and structural analysis

claim: Loss of interaction between SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP loop chimera (LC) and VPS39GFP was observed.
source: We generated chimeras of SARS-CoV-2 and SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a by swapping the 12 amino acid loop sequence between these two proteins and observed loss of the interaction between SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a2x-STREP loop chimera (LC) and VPS39GFP (Figure 6E and F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E, F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a2x-STREP LC displays enhanced interaction with VPS39GFP compared with SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a2x-STREP.
source: Conversely, by substituting the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a 12 amino acid loop into the SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a (SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a2x-STREP LC), we noticed enhanced interaction with VPS39GFP compared with SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a2x-STREP (Figure 6E and G, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E, G and Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: The substitution of the SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a loop into SARS-CoV-1 Orf3a did not fully restore the binding of VPS39 with SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a.
source: However, this substitution did not fully restore the binding of VPS39 with SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a (compare with Figure 6C and F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C and F

claim: Overexpression of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aHALO LC by doxycycline in HEK293 cells did not promote Rab7 accumulation.
source: Overexpression of SARS-CoV-2 Orf3aHALO LC by doxycycline in HEK293 cells did not promote Rab7 accumulation, consistent with its weaker interaction with VPS39 (Figure 6F, H and J).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F, H and J

claim: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3aHALO LC did not promote Rab7 accumulation.
source: SARS-CoV-1 Orf3aHALO LC also did not promote Rab7 accumulation, as one would expect if the Orf3a and VPS39 interaction was fully rescued (Figure 6I).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6I

claim: The binding interface between SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a and VPS39 involves more than the unstructured loop.
source: This is consistent with the co-IP experiments and suggests that the binding interface involves more than the unstructured loop (Figure 6G1 and K, Figure 7A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G, K and Figure 7A

claim: VPS39 is a member of the HOPS complex, a membrane tethering complex that facilitates late endosome or autophagosome fusion with lysosomes.
source: One of these host proteins, VPS39, is a member of the HOPS complex, a membrane tethering complex that facilitates LE or autophagosome (AP) fusion with lysosomes (Balderhaar and Ungermann, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Balderhaar and Ungermann, 2013

claim: Defects in HOPS complex-mediated trafficking lead to the accumulation of late endosomes and autophagosomes.
source: Defects in HOPS complex-mediated trafficking leads to the accumulation of these organelles (Liang et al., 2008; Pols et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2014; Takáts et al., 2014; Aoyama et al., 2012; Messler et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liang et al., 2008; Pols et al., 2013; Jiang et al., 2014; Takáts et al., 2014; Aoyama et al., 2012; Messler et al., 2011

claim: Two SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a residues, S171 and W193, are important for mediating the interaction with VPS39.
source: Two SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a residues, S171 and W193, were identified to be important for mediating this interaction (Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2021

claim: The endocytic pathway is the primary mode of viral egress for several β-coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2.
source: Several recent studies have implicated the endocytic pathway as the primary mode of viral egress for several β-coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, and that Orf3a may mediate this process (Ghosh et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ghosh et al., 2020 and Chen et al., 2021

claim: VPS39 knockdown in SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a overexpressing cells reduces the localization of LAMP1 vesicles near the plasma membrane.
source: In particular, VPS39 knockdown in SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a overexpressing cells reduces the localization of LAMP1 vesicles near the PM, and concomitantly diminishes recruitment of protein complexes involved in Lyso-PM trafficking (Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2021

claim: VPS39 is necessary for SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a-mediated Lyso-PM trafficking.
source: These data suggest that VPS39 is necessary for SARS-CoV-2 Orf3a-mediated Lyso-PM trafficking and implicates the recruitment of the HOPS complex by Orf3a in this process (Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2021
